s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial papules with angiofibroma-like histology
salient_findings: Skin-colored, dome-shaped firm papules over the chin, nose, and perinasal region
Papules increased in size and number since age 18
key_facts: 28-year-old white man
Papules first noticed at age 18
Dozens of skin-colored dome-shaped papules on the face
No hypopigmented macules, periungual fibromas, or Shagreen plaques
Dental examination showed conical-shaped teeth
Biopsy of facial papule showed a dome-shaped lesion with plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels
Electron micrograph showed dermal fibroblast with prominent crystalline inclusions
History of right renal transplant at age 14

differentials: Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinoma
per_call: Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinoma

shortlist.label: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
shortlist.why_kept: Characteristic angiofibromas and renal transplant history

shortlist.label: Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Skin-colored papules and history of renal issues

shortlist.label: Multiple Hamartoma Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Facial papules and possible renal involvement

shortlist.label: Chronic Kidney Disease-Associated Skin Lesions
shortlist.why_kept: History of renal transplant and skin lesions

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple angiofibromas, as indicated by the biopsy results showing dome-shaped lesions with plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels, along with the history of renal transplant which could be related to renal angiomyolipomas, a common feature in TSC, supports this diagnosis. Additionally, the dental findings of conical-shaped teeth can be associated with TSC.

rejected.label: Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic findings such as lung cysts, spontaneous pneumothorax, or renal tumors

rejected.label: Multiple Hamartoma Syndrome
rejected.why: Typically presents with multiple hamartomas, which are not the primary finding in this case

rejected.label: Fibrofolliculoma
rejected.why: While fibrofolliculomas can present as skin-colored papules, the presence of angiofibromas and other systemic findings points towards a more complex syndrome

rejected.label: Chronic Kidney Disease-Associated Skin Lesions
rejected.why: The skin lesions described do not match the typical lesions associated with chronic kidney disease
